newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: RESEARCH ALERT - Sell Hyundai Motor, Kia Motors shrs.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Sell Hyundai Motor, Kia Motors shrs.

text.p: Ssangyong Securities said on Wednesday it has downgraded its recommendations for Hyundai Motor Co Ltd and Kia Motors Corp to "sell" from "hold" because the upside potential for the shares seemed poor.
The securities house said in a report that Hyundai Motor had recently offered buyers free financing plans for its Avante, Sonata III and Marcia models.
"We believe that the plan will trigger similar moves by domestic competitors and greatly intensify competition," Ssangyong said.
South Korea's auto industry was already suffering from stagnant domestic demand and record inventory levels, it said.
"Although share prices have already corrected sharply, we downgrade our recommendation....to "sell" from "hold", believing that upside potential is non-existent," it said.
Ssangyong forecast that Hyundai Motor would see a net profit of 64.5 billion won on a revenue of 11.5 trillion in 1996, compared with 156.7 billion won on 10.34 trillion.
Kia Motors was seen posting a net profit of 5.4 billion won on sales of 6.35 trillion. It netted 11.5 billion won on sales of 5.69 trillion in 1995.
In late morning trading on Wednesday, Hyundai shares were trading unchanged from Tuesday's close of 26,600 won, while Kia shares were up 300 won to 16,000.
